title: Portable technical formulas and owner-bound learned labels form separate semantic layers
summary: Use GDT459's exact event split to distinguish reusable operation/address formulas from learned local names without treating either layer as a translated lexicon.

design.mechanism: A complete surface belongs either to a portable technical formula layer reused in running text or to an owner-bound learned nomenclator layer selected by local image/register context.
design.unit: Complete whole events with exact surface recurrence, running-text recipe evidence, owner context and learned-label status.
design.contrast: Portable formula versus learned local label, with a single-layer lexical model as rival.
design.prediction: Repeated running formulas preserve one recipe across contexts, while learned labels remain owner-bound and need not recur as formulas; a single-layer model predicts no systematic separation after surface frequency controls.
design.falsifier: If recurrence and owner context do not separate the two populations under held surface and section controls, the two-layer semantic claim fails.
design.scope: GDT459 cached 183 events; owner and recipe endpoints are inherited working annotations, not independent lexical bindings; availability_unknown.
design.related: Near GDT459, IDEA000024/25 and existing owner-conditioned/register families; it is a layer distinction, not a new name or object gloss.
design.countermodel: A frequency or section effect can make singleton labels and repeated formulas appear separate even when every whole has one portable role.

design_source_evidence.quote:
# GDT459 — local nomenclator content atlas

## Result

The old `LOCAL_ADDRESS` bucket was too coarse. The 183 events split cleanly
enough to support the mixed system we have been looking for:

| reading tier | events | interpretation |
|---|---:|---|
| exact running formula | 61 | identical surface has one invariant recipe in running text |
| attested recipe under a new surface | 7 | minimal segmentation reproduces an observed recipe |
| short/repeated provisional composition | 8 | bounded new composition; factor reader does not stop |
| learned whole nomenclator label | 107 | owner-bound object/station/name card |

Thus 76 events (55 surfaces) carry address formulae, while 107 events (107
surfaces) are learned whole labels. All retained whole labels are singletons in
this address set. That singleton tail is not a failure of the compositional
model: it is exactly the learned nomenclator layer expected beside a compact
technical code.
